independent_run.meaning: Verifier executed successfully and reached a negative qualification decision.

decisive_hard_negative.setup: Create two distinct kernel_candidate_state_t objects from the same committed state over the same interval, giving both the same public F-KT lineage, origin revision and interval. Materialize physically distinct surface-evaporation results by using different admitted capacity-provider values. Commit candidate A, then finalize prepared result B using accepted receipt A.
decisive_hard_negative.observed: Accepted publication returned OK and ready for B with receipt A.

root_cause: F-PM10 binds publication provenance only to the current public F-KT tuple lineage_id + origin_revision + interval. That tuple is not an exact trial/candidate identity: multiple candidate objects can share it. The accepted commit receipt therefore cannot distinguish distinct same-tuple candidate/result instances.
scope_implication: FPM09-G01 is not closed under the strict exact-candidate requirement. FPM09-G02 therefore cannot pass and FPM09-G03 canonical admission must not start.
required_remediation_property: Introduce or expose an immutable exact candidate/attempt provenance identity that is created with the candidate, survives into the accepted commit receipt, is carried by the candidate-bound surface result, and is checked at publication. The mechanism must remain transaction-local/runtime metadata, not physical persistent column state, and must not alter mass booking or surface-evaporation physics.
nonclaims: This evidence does not prescribe a particular token-generation implementation.
This evidence does not authorize canonical admission.
This evidence does not invalidate existing admitted surface-evaporation calculation or mass closure; it blocks accepted-publication completion.
